title: Japan Ku-area of Tokyo CPI (March 2027, preliminary) + FY2026 Tokyo fiscal yearly average
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table by this session. Against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks', the LAST row parses exactly as ['February', 'March 19', 'March', 'March 26', '2026 fiscal yearly average of Ku-area of Tokyo'] — i.e. the Tokyo March-2027 preliminary CPI releases 2027-03-26. The Remarks cell belongs to THIS release, not to the 2027-03-19 national one on the same row: the Bureau's remark attaches to whichever column it names, exact on all six remarks in the table ('of Japan' to the national column, 'of Ku-area of Tokyo' to the Tokyo column), and the arithmetic agrees — a fiscal-year average needs the final month of its own period in its own geography, and Japan's FY2026 ends 2027-03-31. 2027-03-26 is a Friday and is clear of Japanese public holidays per the Cabinet Office's own list (www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv, HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS, fetched by this session the same day; the 2027 equinox holidays are 2027-03-21 and its substitute 2027-03-22). Filed estimate on three counts, identical to its sibling rows: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page's own last-update stamp is 2026-01-23. The 08:30 JST release time is the Statistics Bureau's standing convention and is NOT asserted in this entry's title
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2027-03-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and it is tracked because it carries the headline that its same-row sibling does NOT. The 2027-03-19 national February print (japan-cpi-2027-03-19, estimate) turns out to be the plainest release on the published schedule — one monthly national index, no annual, no fiscal-annual, no rebasing note — because the row's Remarks cell attaches to this Tokyo release instead. FT-japan-cpi-2027-03-19-3 registers that column rule, scored 2027-03-27. Two further things make this entry worth carrying. (1) FY2026 (2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31) is the LAST FISCAL YEAR UNTOUCHED BY THE FOOD CONSUMPTION-TAX CUT that takes effect 2027-04-01 (japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01, estimate, sized at -1.19pp on core from the Bureau's own 2025-base weight table), so the fiscal-year averages of this cycle are the clean pre-cut benchmark. (2) The corresponding FY2026 average FOR JAPAN attaches, by the same column rule, to the national March-2027 print — the first row past the end of the published table, with NO KNOWN RELEASE DATE. The japan-cpi-2027-03-19 session deliberately declined to derive it: national release dates move up to five days year-on-year (February data went 2026-03-24 to 2027-03-19), so a weekday convention is not a source. A next pulse that finds the Bureau has refreshed its schedule page should file that entry. Impact is LOW: no house playbook is keyed to Japanese prices, symbols is empty. Note the timing quirk this release inherits — Japanese cash markets close 2027-03-22 for the equinox substitute holiday, so the week of the corridor has one fewer session than a US reader expects.
